comment: Every configuration SlimServe supports. Nothing outside this file is a
legal run: the CLI refuses a profile that is not listed, a quant that is
not listed under that profile's model, and a platform that is not listed
under that profile. Engine settings here are the tested ones -- see the

glm52-vision.title: GLM-5.2-Vision
glm52-vision.shared_note: The mmproj is found by globbing the text GGUF's directory and its parent, so it must sit at the repo root while the shards live in antirez-routed/.

IQ2_XXS.title: UD-IQ2_XXS_RoutedIQ2XXS_blk78Q2K
IQ2_XXS.summary: Maximum throughput and longest context. Noticeably weaker at reasoning and precise transcription; fine for classification, routing, short summarization.

Q2_K.title: UD-Q2_K_RoutedQ2K
Q2_K.summary: The tuned path, and what the published throughput numbers were measured on. Best quality that still fits two MI300X with a large KV pool.

Q4_K.title: UD-Q4_K_RoutedQ4K
Q4_K.summary: Reach for this when the task is precision-sensitive: multi-step tool use, code, math, or reading small text out of images. Quantization error compounds across reasoning steps in a way it does not in summarization.

speculator.note: DSpark draft. Speculation costs quality nothing -- the verifier accepts or rejects every draft token -- so it is on by default.

dsv4-flash.title: DeepSeek-V4-Flash
dsv4-flash.shared_note: Text only -- this model has no vision tower, so there is no projector to fetch.

MXFP4.title: MXFP4Experts (0731)
MXFP4.summary: The tuned path. Routed experts in OCP MXFP4, read through this fork's own HIP dequant, GEMV and MMQ tile kernels, and the smaller of the two four-GPU builds.

Q4_K.title: Q4KExperts (0731)
Q4_K.summary: Highest quality of the four, imatrix. Every non-expert tensor is identical to the MXFP4 build; only the routed experts differ.

Q4K-tail.title: Layers37-42Q4KExperts (0731)
Q4K-tail.summary: Q4_K on the last six expert layers, IQ2_XXS gate/up with Q2_K down on the rest. Fits two GPUs while keeping the layers nearest the output at higher precision.

IQ2_XXS.title: IQ2XXS-w2Q2K (0731)
IQ2_XXS.summary: Smallest. IQ2_XXS experts with Q2_K down. IQ2_XXS gate/up has no MMQ tile kernel, so this stays on the vector MoE path at every batch size -- a throughput ceiling, not a correctness limit.

kimi-k3.title: Kimi K3
kimi-k3.shared_note: The vision projector is not in antirez's text repo; it comes from unsloth/Kimi-K3-GGUF. BF16 is preferred because the source vision weights are BF16.

IQ2_XXS-Q2_K.title: Kimi-K3-IQ2_XXS-Q2_K
IQ2_XXS-Q2_K.summary: The only published quant: IQ2_XXS gate/up experts with Q2_K down. 896 routed experts, 93 layers, 24 MLA + 69 KDA.

patch.why: The published file sets kimi-k3.vision = false, which is wrong: the model has a vision tower and the loader skips it otherwise.

assembly.note: Concatenate in lexical order, then apply the patch. Needs 799 GiB free on top of the parts unless the parts are removed as it goes.

glm52-2.title: GLM-5.2-Vision on 2 GPUs
glm52-2.summary: The tuned configuration. Leaves six GPUs free for other work.

glm52-4.title: GLM-5.2-Vision on 4 GPUs
glm52-4.summary: Weights shard far enough to reach the full 1M-token ceiling with room for a much larger KV pool.

a100.note: 80 GB cards: the MI300X KV byte table does not apply, so size the pool by utilization. Q2_K weights leave roughly 58 GB across four cards, which is why the ceiling is 4096 rather than 1M.

glm52-8.title: GLM-5.2-Vision on 8 GPUs
glm52-8.summary: Highest aggregate throughput, and the only profile with room for Q4_K plus a large KV pool.

dsv4-2.title: DeepSeek-V4-Flash on 2 GPUs
dsv4-2.summary: Text only. The two smaller expert quants fit two cards, leaving six free.
notes: block_size must be 256: the DeepSeek-V4 sparse MLA backend rejects GLM's 64 with 'no common block size'.
sparse_mla_force_mqa is required, or short prompts take a dense forward the ROCm sparse backend does not implement.
Context comes from the GGUF (1M, yarn over a 65536 base); KV is sized by the default utilization rather than a measured byte budget.
reasoning_parser must be set: this fork defaults it to glm45 for its GLM target, and that parser classifies a whole DeepSeek reply as reasoning, leaving content null for every API client.

dsv4-4.title: DeepSeek-V4-Flash on 4 GPUs
dsv4-4.summary: Text only. Four cards fit every expert quant, including the tuned MXFP4 build.
notes: block_size must be 256: the DeepSeek-V4 sparse MLA backend rejects GLM's 64 with 'no common block size'.
sparse_mla_force_mqa is required, or short prompts take a dense forward the ROCm sparse backend does not implement.
Context comes from the GGUF (1M, yarn over a 65536 base); KV is sized by the default utilization rather than a measured byte budget.
reasoning_parser must be set: this fork defaults it to glm45 for its GLM target, and that parser classifies a whole DeepSeek reply as reasoning, leaving content null for every API client.

k3-6.title: Kimi K3 on 6 GPUs
k3-6.summary: Tensor parallel across six cards; TP4 does not fit. Two GPUs stay idle, so prefer k3-8t on a full machine -- TP8 became servable once the HIP MLA kernel removed the 16-head floor.
notes: kv_cache_dtype must be 'auto': this fork defaults the cache to fp8 for GLM. fp8 loads and answers correctly here but is a net loss, because K3 is a hybrid. Attention pages must be at least as large as the fixed KDA state page, so halving the per-token attention KV doubles the attention block size (960 -> 1920 tokens) to reach the same page size, and every sequence rounds up to that. Measured on TP6: 344,746 cache tokens and 42.1x concurrency at auto, versus 205,824 and 25.1x at fp8_e4m3.
HSA_XNACK=1 is required for this load.

reasoning_parser must be kimi_k3. K3 frames every channel in XTML rather than with <think>, and the generation prompt opens the first channel, so the parser has to start inside it and drop the closing frame. Under any other parser the answer arrives with "<|close|> response <|sep|> <|close|> message <|sep|>" attached, or -- in thinking mode -- lands entirely in reasoning.

k3-8t.title: Kimi K3 on 8 GPUs, one replica
k3-8t.summary: All eight cards on every request: attention tensor-parallel at 12 heads per rank, experts held whole and split 112-per-rank. Expert parallelism is required -- tensor-sharding the experts slices GGUF quant blocks at TP8.
notes: kv_cache_dtype must be 'auto': this fork defaults the cache to fp8 for GLM. fp8 loads and answers correctly here but is a net loss, because K3 is a hybrid. Attention pages must be at least as large as the fixed KDA state page, so halving the per-token attention KV doubles the attention block size (960 -> 1920 tokens) to reach the same page size, and every sequence rounds up to that. Measured on TP6: 344,746 cache tokens and 42.1x concurrency at auto, versus 205,824 and 25.1x at fp8_e4m3.
HSA_XNACK=1 is required for this load.

reasoning_parser must be kimi_k3. K3 frames every channel in XTML rather than with <think>, and the generation prompt opens the first channel, so the parser has to start inside it and drop the closing frame. Under any other parser the answer arrives with "<|close|> response <|sep|> <|close|> message <|sep|>" attached, or -- in thinking mode -- lands entirely in reasoning.

k3-8.title: Kimi K3 on 8 GPUs
k3-8.summary: Four request replicas, TP2 attention within each pair, and all 896 routed experts split 112-per-rank across the eight cards. Uses every GPU, at a smaller per-replica context than k3-6.
notes: Per-rank weights are 145.17 GiB and every rank reports loading 112/896 experts.
Needs a _C_stable_libtorch built from this tree: the MMQ expert-id fix lives in a .cuh, and a stale extension silently zeroes every expert above 255.
